record.original_question: Can we solve an $(n,k,0,kappa)$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $~ O(k^omega + nnz(A)kappa)$ arithmetic operations?

evidence.quote: Can we solve an $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ linear system $Ax=b$ to high accuracy using $\tilde O(k^\omega + \mathrm{nnz}(A)\kappa)$ arithmetic operations?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\omega$ denote the matrix multiplication exponent, and for a matrix $A$ let $\mathrm{nnz}(A)$ denote the number of nonzero entries of $A$. Call a linear system $Ax=b$ an $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ system if $A\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is invertible, has at most $k$ singular values that exceed the smallest singular value by more than a constant factor (equivalently, $A$ can be written as a well-conditioned matrix plus a perturbation of rank at most $k$), the perturbation has rank exactly $k$ with no additional noise term, and the well-conditioned part has condition number at most $\kappa$.

Question: Is there an algorithm that, given such an $(n,k,0,\kappa)$ system $Ax=b$ and a target accuracy $\varepsilon>0$, computes a vector $\widetilde x$ with $\|\widetilde x - A^{-1}b\|\le \varepsilon \|A^{-1}b\|$ using
$$\widetilde O\!\left(k^{\omega} + \mathrm{nnz}(A)\cdot \kappa\right)$$
arithmetic operations, where $\widetilde O(\cdot)$ hides polylogarithmic factors in $n$, $\kappa$, and $1/\varepsilon$?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on multi-level sketched preconditioning (2024) achieves bounds such as Õ(n^{2.065} + k^ω) for solving n×n systems with k outlying singular values, improving prior results but not matching the conjectured Õ(k^ω + nnz(A)·κ) target. No source verified achieving the precise bound; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Faster Linear Systems and Matrix Norm Approximation via Multi-level Sketched Preconditioning
status_evidence.snippet: Solve any n×n linear system that is well-conditioned except for k outlying large singular values in Õ(n^{2.065} + k^ω) time.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress on the problem achieves related but weaker bounds, not the conjectured Õ(k^ω + nnz(A)·κ).

status_evidence.title: Solving Sparse Linear Systems Faster than Matrix Multiplication
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms that solve sparse linear systems asymptotically faster than matrix multiplication for any ω > 2.
status_evidence.claim: Sparse linear system solving faster than matrix multiplication is an active and not fully resolved area.
